intro.t: Which players change team offense and defense most when they are on the floor?

bullets.t: Net Impact shows the on-minus-off PPP gap; Off and Def break it into which end the player affects.

Off Shot and Def Shot cells show 2PT/3PT frequency and accuracy -- use them to check whether efficiency is driven by sustainable shot selection or a hot-hand streak.

paragraphs.t: In this example, Maccabi Tel Aviv is better with Jimmy Clark III on the floor by +28.1 points per 100 possessions.
That comes from offense being +14.4 points better and defense being 13.7 points better (shown as Def -13.7, because lower defensive PPP allowed is better).
With him on court, Maccabi scores 135.5 and allows 101.1. With him off court, they score 121.1 and allow 114.8.

intro.t: Why is a player's on/off impact happening? Break down the Net diff into shooting (eFG%), rebounding (OREB%), turnovers (TOV%), and free-throw pressure (FTR) on both ends.

bullets.t: Each cell shows the ON minus OFF diff, with on-court and off-court values below and a percentile-rank slider.
Read Offense Impact and Defense Impact blocks separately -- a player can help on one end and hurt on the other.
Gray (unranked) cells mean fewer than 100 on-court possessions; factor diffs from small samples are unreliable.
Free throws, their points and their possession are credited to the lineup on the floor when the foul was drawn, including free throws shot after a substitution.
Cross-reference with the Summary view's 2PT/3PT frequency and accuracy splits to check whether a high eFG% is driven by sustainable shot selection or a hot-hand streak.

four_factors.title: How to Read Four Factors (Real Example)

paragraphs.t: Jimmy Clark III (Maccabi Tel Aviv) shows Diff +28.1 with Off Diff +14.4 and Def Diff -13.7.
Offense factors: eFG% Diff +7.7 explains most of the offensive edge, while OREB% Diff -1.3 is slightly negative.
Defense factors: OREB% Diff +2.2 and TOV% Diff +5.8 show opponents rebound and turn the ball over more with Clark on court.

four_factors.caption: Real Four Factors snippet (On/Off Impact)

intro.t: How does the team's shot diet shift with the player on vs off the floor? Each cell shows the ON-minus-OFF change in share of team FGA, with ON | OFF values below. Each group leads with the team eFG% swing -- the efficiency context the diet shares feed into.

bullets.t: eFG% is the ON-minus-OFF change in team effective FG% (offense: higher is better; defense: lower is better). It is computed from the same shooting splits as the diet shares.

Colors follow the league value hierarchy (interior and 3s beat 2PT jumpers): green = shift toward higher-value shots, red = away; the 2PT Jumper column flips, like TOV% in Four Factors. No point-impact estimate is attached -- efficiency itself lives in the Summary and Four Factors views.
Each cell mirrors Four Factors: the Delta headline, on/off percentile dots on the rank bar, and ON | OFF share values below.

Columns follow the play-by-play shot-type tags: Lay+Dunk = attempts tagged lay-up or dunk (the tag describes execution, not court location -- a running floater can be tagged lay-up); 2PT Jumper = attempts tagged 2-point jump-shot. 3PA% is share of all FGA.
Corner 3 Share splits threes into corner vs above-break, using shots with known court location; -- means location unknown.
Cells gray out below 50 team FGA on the ON side -- small samples produce noisy shares.

shot_profile.note: (Ranked: >= 50 team FGA with player on | eFG% + shares of team FGA, Delta = ON - OFF pp | Corner 3 Share uses known-location 3PA, -- = unknown)

popovers.title: 3PT luck and small sample
popovers.trigger: What do '3PT luck' and 'small sample' mean?

p.t: Three-point accuracy swings a lot from game to game. Whether opponents hit their threes while a player is on the court is mostly out of his hands, and so is much of his own team's hot or cold shooting.

Hover any Net number to see what it would be if every three, by both teams, had gone in at the league average. When three-point luck accounts for more than the whole number (removing it flips the sign), it's marked
3PT luck.

Example: Yovel Zoosman, Hapoel Jerusalem, 25-26: +10.6. 3PT shooting added +11.6, mostly opponents shooting threes better with him off the court; without 3-point luck he is at -1.0, so it is marked 3PT luck.
Only three-point accuracy is adjusted: two-pointers, free throws, turnovers and rebounds count as they happened. Each three counts as 3 points, so the effect is slightly overstated.
On/off numbers are noisy: over one season, most of the gap between players is chance. The hover also shows each number
Adjusted for sample size
-- our best estimate once it is pulled toward the team's own rating, more so the fewer possessions it rests on, especially off the court.
When a number stands out (the table's top or bottom 20%) but rests on far fewer possessions than most rows here, it's marked
small sample.

Units overlap by design: a pair's possessions include every lineup that contained the pair, so unit rows do not sum to a team total.
Minutes and possessions indicate sample size. Small samples produce noisy rates.

intro.t: How good is each EuroLeague team, per possession, on each end?

bullets.t: Off PPP is points scored per 100 possessions; Def PPP is points allowed per 100. Net Rtg is the gap.
Minutes are summed from each selected game's canonical lineup segments; pace is possessions per 40 minutes.
Each cell shows the value, the team's rank in it, and the rank change versus the previous matchday.
Colour runs by rank, green best to red worst, so Def PPP colours in reverse -- allowing fewer points is better.
Opponent-strength filters rank opponents over the whole season, so they do not shift as you narrow the date range.

intro.t: What drives each team's rating? Shooting (eFG%), rebounding (OREB%), turnovers (TOV%), and free-throw pressure (FTR) on both ends.

bullets.t: Offence green-high on every factor except TOV%, where fewer is better; defence flips -- green means the team suppresses that factor.
Rates are computed once from summed raw counts, never averaged across games.
TS% uses the Israeli denominator (FGA plus one per shooting-foul trip), not the 0.44 x FTA estimate.
These counts are derived independently of the Israeli league's possession engine. Do not compare the two leagues' numbers directly.

four_factors.note: Green = better for that team. Offence: higher eFG%/OREB%/FTR, lower TOV%. Defence: lower eFG%/OREB%/FTR allowed, higher opponent TOV%.

ul.t: : Points per 100 possessions (points per possession x 100).
: Offensive PPP minus Defensive PPP. Positive = outscoring opponents.
: Estimated offensive or defensive trips. More possessions = more reliable stats.
: True Shooting -- scoring efficiency accounting for 2PT, 3PT, and free throws. Formula: pts / (2 x (FGA + FT trips)).
: Offensive rebound rate -- share of available misses grabbed. On defense, it measures opponent offensive rebounds allowed.
: Turnover rate -- turnovers per possession. Lower is better on offense; higher is better on defense.
: Free throw rate -- FTA / FGA. Measures how often a team or player gets to the line relative to shot attempts.
: Each cell shows 2PT and 3PT frequency (how often that shot type is taken) and accuracy (FG%).
Accuracy is shown as FG% text, colored from
-- lower Def PPP is better, so green means fewer points allowed.
: On offense, lower TOV% is green (fewer turnovers). On defense, higher TOV% is green (more opponent turnovers).
: The player, lineup, or team has too few possessions to rank reliably (below the minimum threshold).

(Four Factors view): The slider shows where a player ranks from 0% to 100% among all players with enough possessions. 50% = league median. Only players above the minimum possession threshold are included in rankings.
: Each team's sequential game number in the season. Useful for filtering to a stretch of games.
: Only include the most recent N games. Mutually exclusive with GN range.
: Filter games by the opponent's league ranking over the selected sample.
(Tabs 2, 3): Limit to close-game possessions based on score margin, time remaining, and lead/trail status. Overtime qualifies by default.
: Minimum possessions to appear in the table. Higher = more stable data but fewer rows.

columnTooltips.Off: Offensive PPP diff: On-court minus Off-court
columnTooltips.Def: Defensive PPP diff: On-court minus Off-court
columnTooltips.Diff: Net PPP impact: On-court minus Off-court
columnTooltips.TS%: True Shooting: pts / (2 x (FGA + FT trips)). A trip is one visit to the line for a personal foul, credited to the lineup that drew it.
columnTooltips.USG%: Usage rate: share of team shot, free-throw, and turnover possessions while on court
columnTooltips.OREB%: Offense: offensive rebounds / available misses. Defense: opponent offensive rebounds allowed / available misses
columnTooltips.On Poss: On-court possessions for this player or split
columnTooltips.ON Poss: On-court possessions for this player or split
columnTooltips.OFF Poss: Off-court possessions for this player or split
columnTooltips.Poss: Number of possessions in this row or split
columnTooltips.Poss On Floor: Total possessions while this player was on the floor
columnTooltips.# Starters: Number of starters in this lineup
columnTooltips.GN: Team's sequential game number this season
columnTooltips.+/-: Point differential while lineup was on court

filterTooltips.min_poss_side: Minimum OFF + DEF possessions to appear in table
filterTooltips.min_on_poss: Minimum ON-court possessions for percentile ranking
filterTooltips.own_starters: Filter by number of starters in the team's lineup
filterTooltips.opp_starters: Filter by number of starters in the opposing lineup
filterTooltips.gn: Sequential game number within a team's season; player and team views both use the team's GN
filterTooltips.last_n: Only include the most recent N games in the selected team context
filterTooltips.opp_strength: Filter games by the opponent's league ranking over the selected sample
filterTooltips.clutch: Limit results to close-game situations based on margin, time remaining, and score status
filterTooltips.group_size: Number of players in each lineup combination (2-5)
filterTooltips.quick_preset: Apply a prebuilt compare split like starters vs bench, clutch vs non-clutch, or date/GN split
filterTooltips.players_on: Every player selected here has to be on the floor
filterTooltips.players_on_any: At least one player selected here has to be on the floor, on top of the box above. Leave it empty to match on the first box alone
filterTooltips.players_off: Skip any lineup containing a player selected here
filterTooltips.min_poss_lineup: Minimum total possessions required for the lineup, team, or compare side to appear

offOrebTooltip: Offensive rebound rate: offensive rebounds / available misses
defOrebTooltip: Opponent offensive rebound rate allowed: opponent offensive rebounds / available misses
